subject.title: MissingAgentHarnessError race: non-atomic harness registry clear+restore during plugin cache cycle

question: Should empty plugin scopes preserve only maintainer-approved always-on harnesses, clear all plugin-owned harnesses, or restore every prior harness during gateway/plugin reloads?
rationale: Current source proves the lifecycle hazard, but choosing the permanent behavior changes plugin disablement, provider routing, and security-boundary semantics; automation should not pick that policy from the issue alone.

options.title: Preserve Approved Always-On Harnesses
options.body: Filter registry preservation to the approved always-on/core harness contract and keep disabled or unscoped plugin-owned harnesses cleared, with loader and gateway tests.

options.title: Restore All Prior Harnesses
options.body: Allow every previous harness to survive an empty active registry, accepting the compatibility and security-boundary tradeoff explicitly.

options.title: Retry Dispatch Only
options.body: Add bounded retry/backoff at dispatch while leaving registry semantics unchanged, but require safeguards so real missing-runtime states still surface clearly.

recommendation.title: Preserve Approved Always-On Harnesses
recommendation.body: Filter registry preservation to the approved always-on/core harness contract and keep disabled or unscoped plugin-owned harnesses cleared, with loader and gateway tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The harness registry was introduced by this owner trail, and the decision crosses agent runtime, plugin loader, and gateway lifecycle boundaries.
